content.value_statement: Tree-sitter projects need repeatable parsing patterns and query guidance. This skill provides practical patterns for AST navigation, queries, visitors, and parser integration.
actual_capabilities: Explains parser setup with the Python tree-sitter bindings.
Shows common AST navigation patterns using child and named child traversal.
Provides tree-sitter query examples for functions, classes, imports, and decorators.
Describes an AST visitor pattern for extracting function names.
Lists common node type names across Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust.
Covers parse error handling, incremental parsing, and integration with code analysis workflows.
limitations: Referenced cookbook documents are not included in the scanned package.
Examples are documentation patterns, not a complete parser implementation.
Language support depends on installed tree-sitter parser packages.
Project-specific query tuning still requires testing on real source files.

use_cases.title: Prototype code extraction
use_cases.description: Create a first pass for extracting functions, classes, imports, and parse errors from source files.

use_cases.title: Standardize AST traversal
use_cases.description: Use visitor and query patterns to make tree traversal consistent across a parsing project.

use_cases.title: Plan language support
use_cases.description: Compare common node types and parser setup needs before adding a new language.

prompt_templates.title: Identify parser setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tree-sitter patterns skill to outline parser setup for Python. Include parser package needs, source input handling, and basic root node inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Draft extraction queries
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tree-sitter patterns skill to design queries for extracting functions, classes, imports, and decorators from a Python project.

prompt_templates.title: Build visitor flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tree-sitter patterns skill to design an AST visitor workflow that collects function names and records parse errors.

prompt_templates.title: Design multi-language analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the tree-sitter patterns skill to plan a multi-language code analysis pipeline for Python, TypeScript, Go, and Rust.

output_examples.input: Request a plan for extracting functions and imports from Python files.
output_examples.output: A concise parsing plan with parser setup, query targets, error handling, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Ask how to traverse a syntax tree without visiting punctuation nodes.
output_examples.output: Guidance to use named children, a reusable visitor method, and focused extraction methods.

output_examples.input: Ask for performance guidance when parsing edited files repeatedly.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for incremental parsing, specific queries, lazy traversal, and parser version pinning.

best_practices: Test query patterns on representative source files before using them in production.
Handle parse errors and missing nodes as normal cases.
Pin parser package versions so node type behavior remains stable.
anti_patterns: Assuming every source file parses cleanly.
Traversing the full tree when a focused query would answer the question.
Copying node type names between languages without checking each grammar.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design tree-sitter parsing workflows, AST visitors, query patterns, and code extraction plans.

faq.question: Does it install tree-sitter parsers?
faq.answer: No. It describes setup patterns, but parser packages must be installed in the target project.

faq.question: Can it generate project-specific queries?
faq.answer: It can guide query design, but final queries should be tested against the project grammar and sample code.

faq.question: Which languages are referenced?
faq.answer: The skill references Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, and Rust node type examples.

faq.question: Does it include runnable tooling?
faq.answer: No. The scanned package contains documentation examples in SKILL.md.

faq.question: Is it safe for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: The reviewed static hits are Markdown formatting false positives, with no evidence of external command execution.
